DevBot: INCIDENT ALERT: service=decode-streaming severity=page type=GPU_OOM — multiple GPUs in pool `decode-pool-prod` reported OOMs and container restarts. Paging oncall. https://incidents.redwood.ai/1719978888 :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge. Which customers affected?
Lina (support): Seeing elevated 5xx from a small set of requests tied to streaming endpoint. Support ticket #S-4128 opened by AcmeCorp; they saw partial responses and then failures.
Maya (oncall): Thanks Lina. Priya, can you pull runtime logs / KV cache stats?
Priya (runtime): Pushing logs now. Initial glance: repeated cuda errors inside decode workers, then container exits: `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` followed by kube container restart. Also a lot of long-running streams — token counts for some requests spiking to >100k.
Sam (sre): That sounds like runaway generation. Any evidence of max_tokens mismatch or header bypass?
Jonas (infra): Node telemetry shows one node with GPU memory at 100% and repeated OCI kill. Multiple containers on same host hit OOM within 3s of each other. Suggest quarantine node.
Priya (runtime): Confirmed. Logs: ```
[2024-07-31T03:14:12Z] decode_worker[pid=2143] ERROR cuda call failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: invalid device memory access
[2024-07T03:14:12Z] decode_worker[pid=2143] INFO dumping KV cache length=16384 tokens
[2024-07-31T03:14:13Z] systemd: container exited with status 137
```
Maya (oncall): Action list: 1) Quarantine node(s) 2) Apply temporary request-level max_tokens enforcement 3) Patch routing to fallback smaller model variant 4) Customer comm. Who can run quarantine?
Jonas (infra): I'll cordon + drain the affected node. Command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```
Jonas (infra): Starting drain now. Expect some restarts as pods reschedule.
Priya (runtime): While Jonas is draining, we should enforce per-request token cap at the ingress layer to stop existing runaway streams. We can inject an HTTP filter to drop requests with header `x-max-tokens` > 4096.
Sam (sre): I can push a temporary Envoy route with the following LUA filter: ```lua
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local h = request_handle:headers():get("x-max-tokens")
  if h and tonumber(h) > 4096 then
    request_handle:logInfo("dropping oversized max_tokens header")
    request_handle:respond({["status"] = "413", ["body"] = "token cap exceeded"})
  end
end
```
Sam (sre): Rolling to 3 edge nodes now.
Lina (support): Drafting a one-line customer note: "We're seeing GPU-level OOMs impacting streaming for some workloads. We're applying emergency rate and token caps and will follow up with mitigation details." Want sign-off from Maya/Victor.
Victor (cust-succ): Thumbs up. Also coordinate with AcmeCorp, they may have a misconfigured SDK. Ask for reproducer including request headers.
Maya (oncall): Good. Priya — any quick telemetry we can attach to support ticket?
Priya (runtime): I'll attach a KV cache dump and per-request token histogram for the last 30m. Also flagged a correlation: many failing requests include `x-client-sdk-version: 1.2.0-beta` and an `x-max-tokens` header set to 999999. Could be a client bug that bypasses server-side limit.
Sam (sre): That's our vector — client header bypass + no enforcement in the past -> runaway generation -> KV cache blowup -> CUDA illegal address during kv indexing -> kernel crash -> container OOM.
Jonas (infra): Node drain completed for gpu-node-17. It moved 42 pods; 6 pods failed to schedule immediately due to GPU capacity. I'm enabling burst capacity on Dedicated pool to accept reschedules: `infractl capacity set decode-pool-prod --burst 2`
Maya (oncall): Priya, can we switch requests to a smaller model variant automatically when a node OOMs?
Priya (runtime): Yes. I'm enabling a routing rule now to prefer `model:decoder-lite` for any request coming through the affected AZ. Config snippet I'm applying: ```yaml
routing_policy:
  - match: {region: us-west-2, pool: decode-pool-prod}
    action: fallback
    fallback_model: decoder-lite
```
Priya (runtime): Applied. Telemetry shows a drop in memory pressure on rescheduled pods.
DevBot: Deployment bot: envoy-lua-filter rollout started on 3 nodes by Sam.
Sam (sre): Envoy filter in place. We already dropped ~120 requests that exceeded cap. CPU for decode pool dropping back to baseline.
Lina (support): Sent initial message to AcmeCorp requesting SDK logs + sample request. They replied: "we upgraded to 1.2.0-beta yesterday and saw an abnormal spike, attaching request dump" — their dump includes `x-max-tokens: 999999` and `stream: true`.
Victor (cust-succ): Looping in their engineering. Also told them temporary mitigation is in place and asking for rollback to stable SDK 1.1.x while we investigate.
Maya (oncall): Any sign this is a kernel/driver mismatch (recent node kernel patch)?
Jonas (infra): Not seeing new kernel updates. There was a recent container runtime update on two nodes that may have surfaced a latent device pointer bug. I'm opening infra issue INF-789 to track.
Priya (runtime): For long term, we need: 1) enforce server-side max_tokens 2) hard token ceilings at routing 3) better KV cache eviction for pathological prefixes 4) add guardrails to kernel/api calls to avoid illegal memory access when KV indexing grows beyond expected.
Sam (sre): I'll prepare a runbook step to quarantine nodes faster and to toggle the envoy filter as a mitigation toggle.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact summary for postmortem: AcmeCorp saw ~2.1k failed streaming requests over 40m window; system dropped requests and some customers saw degraded latency. No data loss beyond dropped responses.
Lina (support): Logged customer update and scheduled a follow-up for 1pm PST.
Priya (runtime): Also capturing crash dumps and core logs; uploading to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1719978888/ . Adding pointer to ticket.
DevBot: Incident severity escalated to Sev2 per oncall.
Jonas (infra): I've isolated 3 nodes for deeper host-level forensic. They're out of rotation. Leaving a small set of nodes in warm standby for traffic.
Sam (sre): Quick mitigation checklist we executed: - cordon+drain offending node - apply envoy token cap - enable fallback model - increase burst capacity - notify customer - collect dumps
Maya (oncall): Good. Next actions: Priya to create runtime PR for server-side max_tokens enforcement; Sam to add ENV toggle to ops console for emergency token cap; Jonas to run forensic and roll back container runtime if needed; Lina/Victor to continue customer comms.
Priya (runtime): I'll open PR and link in thread. Expect it in ~90m.
Sam (sre): I'll put the Envoy filter toggle in the console within 2 hours and document in runbook.
Victor (cust-succ): Customer acknowledged rollback to 1.1.x and thanks for quick mitigation; will keep ticket open until they validate.
Maya (oncall): Marking this thread as ongoing. Please update this thread with any critical changes. If we reach stable state for 30m, we'll downgrade severity.
OpsBot: autoscaler: burst capacity change applied for decode-pool-prod by Jonas at 2024-07-31T03:48:22Z.
DevBot: Closing note: postmortem owner required. Please nominate.
Sam (sre): I'll own the postmortem with Priya.
Maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. Keeping page open until confirmed stable. :white_check_mark:
